I've played arms race and death match quite a bit to get a feel for guns but still get my ass kicked in regular matches. Just looking for tips to get better and avoid being yelled at before I start competitive. Any advice?

No problem :D

Just want to make this /v/globaloffensive grow bigger and if I can help people ... Why not :)

I know WouWou already showed you a ton of tips, but what I did was just play the game. Jump into competitive without worrying about your rank. It's always smart to learn the complete basic before hopping in, but if you can go to a site, kill people, and understand the economy system, playing the game is the best way in my opinion. Nothing beats constant experience in a real scenario. Besides that, work on your movement in KZ/Surf/Bhop servers and aim in fragshack. I find that my aim gradually got better by playing the game over and over, but movement was specialized in KZ. I don't think I could've learned as good of movement without specific servers for it. My view at CS was why learn to out gun your opponent if you're constantly catching them off guard or from behind? If you have decent aim, spraying someone from behind isn't difficult. If you're trying to carry in competitive though, I'd probably practice entry fragging. Getting a pick or two and clearing a site for your team does wonders when you can't rely on them 100%.

This book is written by Kevin Mahar. It's his debut novel.

I read this because a friend said she needed someone to talk about this book with. It took me forever to get through it, it was slow and the writing without "" was driving me crazy. I thought it was because the book was set in Ireland and being an American meant some of the language and names were a struggle for me to get my head around.

But even after I struggled through that the entire story line (End of pt 1 to the end of the book) was just way more than I could deal with. The story line made me feel like the author wrote a ton of ideas down and was going to draw them from a hat - but instead of stopping at one or two conflicts he dumped the hat out, said fuck it, and proceeded to included everything that could happen to a young boy in one book.

The ending of the book made me go "What the actual Fuck?" when I finished and even months later I still have no idea what happened. I wouldn't recommend this book because it was far from Laugh out loud funny and it was such a struggle to get through that if I'm forced to choose between re-reading this and reading a pamphlet about Genital warts, I would go with the pamphlet.
